Use Cases

Use it this way to get even more out of it.

Knowing the features is just the start. In 3 steps — common scenario → how to use it → the payoff — we'll show you tips you can put to work right away.

🏠

Home tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

Does it take you 10+ minutes every morning just to open and check your tasks one by one, scattered across multiple Backlog projects? And even then, it's not obvious where to start.

💡 How to use it
Automatically sorted by due date, just by opening it

Shown already grouped into overdue, today, within a week, and more

Quick filters plus search narrow it down to what you need to do right now

One-click filter chips and full-text search narrow things down in an instant

🎉 The payoff

Your morning check shrinks to under a minute, and nothing slips through the cracks.

📅

Calendar tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

Ever hit month-end and suddenly realized, “Wait, this project is also due this week...”? A flat task list alone makes it hard to spot deadline clustering across the month.

💡 How to use it
Visualize deadlines with the monthly calendar

This month's and next month's tasks line up in their due-date cells, so you can spot deadline clustering at a glance

Risk level is shown automatically by color

Overdue in red, due today in orange. The 7-week rolling view shows last week too

🎉 The payoff

Spot deadline clustering early, and get started ahead of time with room to spare.

⊞

Matrix tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

Once your assigned tasks pile up to 20 or 30, it's hard to tell where to even start — so you end up handling whatever catches your eye first and pushing off the important work.

💡 How to use it
Auto-plotted by urgency x importance

Just open the Matrix view and tasks are auto-plotted into 4 quadrants

Work through it starting from the top-right quadrant

Click a quadrant to list just that priority's tasks in the right panel

🎉 The payoff

Zero time wasted deciding what's next. No more pushing off the important tasks.

🌳

Gantt tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

On projects with multiple people involved, when someone's task slips, it's unclear how it ripples to other tasks — and the scheduling meeting drags on.

💡 How to use it
Drag the bar to change the due date

Drag start and due dates directly, and they're reflected in Backlog instantly

Automatically proposes a schedule shift for downstream tasks

Dependent downstream tasks shift automatically after confirmation. The lightning line makes delays obvious at a glance

🎉 The payoff

Schedule adjustments are done entirely within the Gantt view.

🗂

Kanban tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

Going around the standup asking “How's it going, so-and-so?” one person at a time eats up most of the meeting on its own.

💡 How to use it
Just share your screen and everyone's status is right there

The whole team's progress is visualized across Open, In Progress, Processed, and Done columns

Change status right there with D&D

Just drag a card to move it, and it's instantly reflected in Backlog — no more manual status reports

🎉 The payoff

No more going around asking everyone one by one — your standup wraps up in 5 minutes.

👑

Dashboard tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

As a project lead, are you stuck manually tallying each project's progress and delays, one by one, every week just to put together your weekly report?

💡 How to use it
The Cross-Space Summary gives you a bird's-eye view of every project

Health score, completion rate, and delay hours are aggregated automatically for side-by-side comparison

At-risk projects are flagged automatically by color

Flags of 🔴 for a 50%+ delay rate and 🟡 for 20%+ make it obvious which project to tackle first

🎉 The payoff

Prep for your weekly report wraps up in minutes, so you can get a head start on at-risk projects.

🎮

Backlog Quest tips & tricks

Use Cases
😩 Common scenarios

Task work can easily feel like a chore, and it's hard to stay motivated through the daily grind.

💡 How to use it
Just use Backlog as usual, and it turns into experience points

Logging in, creating/editing/completing tasks, and posting comments all become experience points for your character

Boss battles and unlocking achievements make for a nice little break

Boss battles every 10 levels, gear collection, hidden bosses, and achievement badges give your daily work natural milestones

🎉 The payoff

Handling tasks itself becomes something to look forward to, keeping your motivation up over the long run.

See how it fits into your everyday routine.

The more you know about it, the more useful Backlog My Tasks becomes.
